one_month_reasoning: AMD's own Q3 2026 report is expected on 2026-11-03 (after the 2026-10-30 window closes; AMD reported Q3 on Nov 4 last year), so the largest single catalyst falls just outside the window. Inside the window: hyperscaler Q3 reports with capex commentary (Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet, Amazon, typically the last week of October) and TSMC's mid-October results; these are sector read-throughs that could move AMD 5-10% either way, and after Q2 all signals were for rising capex (Meta and Microsoft are named Helios customers). Pre-earnings run-ups are common but the stock is already near its 52-week high ($639) after +281% in a year, and the World Labs all-stock deal ($8.2B, ~1% dilution, announced 2026-09-28) was received positively. With no scheduled company-specific event, I stay close to a symmetric lognormal centred at ~$606 (a hair of positive drift) with monthly sigma ~19.5% (72% annual realized / ~3.7).

fair_value.method: Blend of (a) 30x a Sep-2027 NTM non-GAAP EPS of ~$20.5 less ~4% expected warrant dilution (~$590, 60% weight) and (b) management's long-term EPS path (~$30 by 2030, 25x exit, discounted 3 years at 11%, plus ~$6/share net cash ~ $555, 40% weight) = ~$580.

Stock trades ~39-40x FY27 consensus today with Street average target ~$618; as growth decelerates from ~80% EPS growth (FY26) to ~40% I assume de-rating to ~30x forward, roughly a PEG of 0.75, in line with where large AI semis have traded at similar growth.

OpenAI and Meta each hold $0.01 warrants for up to 160M shares (320M total vs 1,632M basic) vesting on GW purchase milestones and escalating stock thresholds (final Meta tranche $600); none vested at 2026-06-27. By Sep-2027 first-GW tranches may vest; consensus diluted share counts (~1.66B) likely exclude them. 4% ~ 65M shares expected by then.

bear.story: AI capex digestion in 2027 or Helios/MI450 slips; the first-GW deployments (Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta) land late or smaller, customers seek vendor financing (risk flagged in 10-Q), $30B of purchase commitments turn into inventory risk, memory costs squeeze client; EPS ~$12-13 at ~25x.

base.story: DC roughly doubles in 2027 as guided, FY27 EPS ~$15-17, the Street moves to FY28 EPS ~$21-22 and the multiple compresses to ~30x; some warrant dilution. The stock grinds sideways-to-up from an already full price.

bull.story: Helios ramps ahead of plan; revenue per GW in the double-digit billions across 3+ multi-GW customers pushes FY27 EPS toward the $20 high estimate and FY28 toward $28-30, with the market holding ~35x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$380 the stock would trade at ~24x FY27 consensus EPS ($15.57), roughly a market-multiple for a company guiding DC to more than double. That would most likely mean the 2027 Helios/MI450 ramp or the multi-GW customer commitments (OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic) have slipped or been cut, not ordinary volatility (it is ~37% below today, about one annual sigma of a de-risked 55-60% vol).

reasoning: Primary documents show a business in a steep up-cycle: Q2'26 revenue $11.5B (+50%), DC $6.7B (+107%), non-GAAP EPS $1.66; Q3 guided to $13.0B at 56% GM; on the call management said DC will more than double in 2027, server CPU will grow >70%, revenue per GW is in the 'double-digit billions', and it will 'significantly exceed' the $20 EPS target. Consensus FY27 EPS has jumped from $13.10 to $15.57 in 90 days. Against that, the stock already sits at ~39x FY27 EPS after +281%, and filings the recaps skip show ~20% potential dilution from the OpenAI/Meta $0.01 warrants (final Meta tranche needs a $600 price, now met, so price conditions are no longer a brake), $30.3B of purchase commitments, $4.75B of new debt in August, and a new $8.2B all-stock acquisition of a pre-revenue AI lab (capital-allocation signal). My fair value (~$580) is close to spot: rising earnings are offset by multiple compression and dilution over 12 months. So I centre the 12-month distribution at a median of ~$612 (slight positive drift from earnings momentum) with log-sigma 0.60, a little below the 72% realized vol because the run-up inflated it, but well above the large-cap base rate given the concentration and cyclicality. That gives P(>=604) ~0.51, a ~27% chance below $423 (the bear case) and ~25% above $906 (the bull case), consistent with the 25/50/25 scenarios (probability-weighted mean ~$640). The 1-month view is near-neutral because AMD's own earnings (2026-11-03) fall just after the window. Research note: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints were unavailable (plan limits and rate limits), so consensus comes from web aggregators.
